citation: Savage, R., Abrami, P. C., Piquette, N., Wood, E., Deleveaux, G., Sanghera-Sidhu, S., & Burgos, G. (2013). A (Pan-Canadian) cluster randomized control effectiveness trial of the ABRACADABRA web-based literacy program. Journal of Educational Psychology, 105(2), 310-328. https://doi.org/10.1037/a0031025
report_number: Journal of Educational Psychology, 105(2), 310-328; DOI 10.1037/a0031025; ERIC EJ1007934
design: Cluster-randomized effectiveness RCT; assignment at the classroom (Teacher/Class) level; 74 matched classrooms (37 ABRA intervention, 37 control), 1,067 students (549 intervention, 518 control); Pan-Canadian (3 provincial sites). Teachers received a full day of training plus extended in-class just-in-time support (RA present first 4 weeks; monthly meetings) and delivered the ABRACADABRA (ABRA) web-based early-literacy program to their regular classrooms for ~20 hr/child over one semester vs business-as-usual ELA. Whole-sample analyses pool kindergarten (12 paired classes, n=24) and Grade 1/2 (25 paired classes, n=50); some measures (fluency/comprehension) administered to Grade 1/2 only. Subject = reading/literacy; grades K-2. Impact via 3-level HLM (pupil/classroom/school) with pretest attainment and chronological age as covariates.
problems: All outcomes are reading/literacy (Reading). Single intervention arm (ABRA vs control), so all effect sizes share row_id 103. PREFERRED estimates use the HLM classroom-level 'Intervention condition' coefficient (Table 2, p.319) as the pretest- and cluster-adjusted raw-scale impact b, standardized by the unadjusted pooled posttest SD from Table 1 (p.318): g = J*(b/s); g_se = J*(SE_b/s). This treats the HLM SE as already cluster-adjusted (cluster_adjusted=true). EXCEPTIONS/AMBIGUITIES: (1) GRADE Sentence Comprehension - the classroom-level 'Intervention condition' coefficient/SE cell is BLANK in the published Table 2 (the classroom-level column for this measure appears shifted up one row in the typesetting), so its g was computed from raw posttest means/SDs (Table 1) instead and is NOT cluster-adjusted; central correction via ICC would be needed but no ICC is reported. (2) GRADE Listening Comprehension was analysed on 66 of 74 paired classrooms (8 K classes missing the subtest by error); exact student n for that subset is not reported, so n_t/n_c use the full-sample 549/518 as an approximation (flagged per-effect). (3) No ICC / design-effect ICC is reported anywhere in the paper (NEVER guessed). (4) n_clusters recorded as total classrooms in the analytic sample for each measure (74 whole-sample; 66 for Listening Comp; 50 for Grade1/2 fluency/retell; 46 for Grade1/2 GRADE comprehension). (5) Table 3 reports a SECONDARY, NON-randomized breakdown of the intervention group by implementation-fidelity level (entry/adoption/adaptation vs control); those are not randomized arms and were NOT extracted as separate contrasts per spec (skip non-randomised subsets). (6) The paper itself does not print Hedges' g or Cohen's d in the main impact tables (Table 3's 'effect sizes' described in text were not numerically tabulated in the version on disk); g values here are computed by the extractor. (7) Fry Words is a researcher-adapted word-reading test (from Fry's Instant Word List); all other measures are standardized/independent (CTOPP, DIBELS, GRADE). Several Grade 1/2 reading measures (fluency, retell, sentence/passage comprehension) numerically favored CONTROL on raw posttest means but the pretest-adjusted HLM impacts are near zero/non-significant - the divergence reflects baseline differences absorbed by the ANCOVA-style HLM.
